# Specillum

> Specillum is an open-source MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets AI coding agents such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and Cursor use your real, logged-in Chrome, while giving every agent its own isolated browser window ("pod"). Agents cannot see or touch your tabs or each other's tabs. Apache-2.0, by Jason (@jasonwpgml).

Key facts:
- One shared Chrome ("station") with a dedicated profile: log in once with `npx specillum open`, and every agent reuses those live sessions.
- Each MCP connection gets a pod: a separate Chrome window. Tools only operate on pages inside that pod, including new tabs and popups it opens.
- Pods close automatically when the agent disconnects.
- Token-efficient snapshot: visible interactive elements as one line each with refs like `[e12]`.
- Tools: pod_status, pod_window, navigate, history, snapshot, read, click, type, press, select, hover, scroll, wait, screenshot, dialog, tabs, evaluate.
- Works with any MCP client over stdio. Built on Playwright (playwright-core) over the Chrome DevTools Protocol.
- Tested on Windows; macOS and Linux browser paths are included.
